title: Efficacy of Tecovirimat for the Treatment of Mpox Virus Infection in Humans: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Tecovirimat has been widely used for the treatment of mpox despite limited evidence supporting its efficacy. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tecovirimat for this purpose. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to June 5, 2026 for RCTs comparing tecovirimat with placebo or standard care in patients with laboratory-confirmed mpox. Primary outcomes were time to clinical resolution of skin lesions, clinical resolution by day 28-29, and 28-day all-cause mortality. Hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Two low-risk-of-bias RCTs involving 941 participants were included. Tecovirimat did not shorten the time to clinical resolution of skin lesions compared with placebo (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.52-2.31, GRADE: moderate) or increase the lesion resolution by day 28-29 (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.92-1.08, GRADE: high). No statistical heterogeneity was observed (I 2 = 0% for both outcomes). Mortality at day 28 was rare in both trials, precluding meta-analysis. Virological clearance, pain-related outcomes, and serious adverse events were also comparable between treatment groups. In conclusion, current randomized evidence does not support routine tecovirimat use to accelerate clinical recovery or improve mortality rates in patients with mpox, while further evidence is needed to determine whether selected high-risk populations may benefit from antiviral therapy.

title: Global mpox outbreak dynamics during and after the 2024–2026 public health emergency
abstract: The second WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) for mpox was declared on 14 August 2024 after clade Ib monkeypox virus emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and spread rapidly across Africa and internationally. The PHEIC ended on 5 September 2025, and the Africa CDC Public Health Emergency of Continental Security was lifted on 22 January 2026. This study characterised global and Africa-specific mpox epidemiology across the full second PHEIC cycle and immediate post-emergency period, from January 2024 to February 2026. A retrospective surveillance analysis was conducted using the WHO Global Mpox Trends dashboard exported data, supplemented by WHO situation reports S32–S64 and international and national surveillance reports. Analyses included negative binomial segmented regression, travel-linked pathway analysis, exploratory analysis of documented secondary transmission after travel-linked detection, and descriptive statistics. Models used reported case counts with log population offsets; reported case-rate ratios therefore reflect reported case rates rather than true infection incidence. Between January 2024 and February 2026, 82,738 confirmed cases and 306 deaths were reported to WHO globally (case fatality ratio 0.37%). The PHEIC period accounted for 74.0% of cases, peaking at 7,405 cases in May 2025. In total, 163 clade-specific importation or travel-linked detection events were documented across 41 countries within the primary analytic cutoff; documented secondary transmission occurred in 25 (15.3%) events across 16 countries. Within DRC, 200 health zones recorded 144,035 total reported cases and 2,047 deaths (case fatality ratio 1.42%); these aggregate suspected/clinically compatible and confirmed cases. The top 20 health zones accounted for 45.4% of national burden. Reported transmission declined after the May 2025 peak but persisted beyond PHEIC termination. Emergency termination marked an administrative transition, not the end of mpox transmission. The post-emergency period requires sustained surveillance, maintained diagnostic capacity, targeted response in persistent transmission settings, and equitable access to vaccines and countermeasures.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在描述第二次世界卫生组织国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(PHEIC)期间全球和非洲特定的 猴痘 的特征,该事件于 2024 年 8 月 14 日宣布,当时 Ib 分支猴痘病毒在刚果民主共和国(DRC)出现并在非洲和国际范围内迅速传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用世卫组织全球 猴痘 趋势仪表板导出的数据进行回顾性 监测 分析,并辅以世卫组织情况报告 S32-S64 以及国际和国家 监测 报告。该研究覆盖 41 个国家,包括 163 个特定分支的输入或与旅行相关的检测事件。
elements_zh.methods: 分析包括负二项式分段回归、旅行相关路径分析、旅行相关检测后记录的次要 传播 的探索性分析以及描述性统计。
elements_zh.main_results: 2024年1月至2026年2月,全球向世卫组织报告确诊病例82,738例,死亡306例(病死率0.37%)。PHEIC 期间占病例数的 74.0%,在 2025 年 5 月达到峰值 7,405 例。模型使用报告病例数和对数人口偏移量;因此,报告的病例率反映的是报告的病例率,而不是真实的感染情况 发病率。报告的 传播 在 2025 年 5 月的峰值后有所下降,但在 PHEIC 终止后仍持续存在。在刚果民主共和国境内,200个卫生区共报告病例144,035例,死亡2,047例(病死率1.42%);这些汇总了疑似/临床兼容和确诊病例。排名前20的卫生区占全国负担的45.4%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,PHEIC期间占大多数病例,但猴痘在正式终止后仍然持续存在,表明紧急状态的结束标志着行政过渡,而不是猴痘传播的停止。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要持续的 监测、保持诊断能力、在持续的 传播 环境中进行有针对性的响应,以及在紧急情况后时期公平获得 疫苗 和对策。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于报告的病例数,这可能无法反映真实的感染情况 发病率,并且病例率比是基于对数人口偏移量。证据是中等的,因为它来自 监测 数据,不包括直接的生物学或临床测量。

title: Deep Learning and Computational Modeling for Epitope-Focused Immunogen Design Targeting Monkeypox
abstract: Abstract Monkeypox (MPX), now widely called mpox, is a zoonotic orthopoxvirus infection that has moved from a neglected tropical disease to a global public health concern. Live-attenuated smallpox vaccines offer cross-protection, but they are produced in limited quantities, are unevenly distributed, and are not suited to every recipient. These constraints motivate the search for rationally designed, epitope-focused immunogens that can be produced at scale and tailored to emerging viral variants. This article describes an in silico framework that combines amino acid feature engineering, classical machine learning (ML) benchmarking, and a deep neural network (DNN) to predict potential T-cell and B-cell epitopes from the MPX virus proteome (VP). Epitope and non-epitope sequences, together with antigen information, were collected from public immunology and virology databases, encoded numerically, and described by a panel of 84 amino acid features. Hierarchical heat-map clustering based on Pearson correlation identified 44 of the 84 features as redundant, and these were removed before modeling. Twenty-eight ML algorithms were then screened; the five best performers, namely Random Forest, Label Spreading, Decision Tree, Label Propagation and Extra Trees, were compared using accuracy, F1 score and the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), the last two being appropriate for imbalanced data. A DNN with fully connected dense layers, trained by back-propagation with the Adam optimizer, was evaluated with two and four hidden layers. The four-layer network converged faster in terms of loss, while accuracy did not differ significantly between architectures across training epochs. According to the held-out test data, the DNN outperformed the traditional ML models and other deep learning approaches. Because the framework is not specific to one pathogen, it can in principle be retrained to support vaccine design against other emerging infectious diseases. We discuss the biological rationale, methodological choices, limitations, and the experimental validation steps required to move from computational candidates to a multivalent MPX immunogen.

The study highlights the potential of this framework for vaccine design against emerging viral variants, although it is limited to computational analysis without experimental validation. The findings suggest that the framework could be adapted for other pathogens, but its application to mpox requires further biological testing.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 猴痘 (MPX) 现在广泛称为 猴痘,是一种人畜共患的 正痘病毒 感染,已从一种被忽视的热带疾病转变为全球公共卫生问题。这些限制促使人们寻找合理设计、针对表位的免疫原,这些免疫原可以大规模生产并针对新出现的病毒变体进行定制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究描述了一个计算机框架,该框架结合了氨基酸特征工程、经典机器学习 (ML) 基准测试和深度神经网络 (DNN),以预测 MPX 病毒蛋白质组 (VP) 中潜在的 T 细胞和 B 细胞表位。
elements_zh.methods: 表位和非表位序列以及抗原信息是从公共免疫学和病毒学数据库中收集的,进行数字编码,并由一组 84 个氨基酸特征进行描述。基于 Pearson 相关性的分层热图聚类将 84 个特征中的 44 个识别为冗余,并在建模之前将其删除。然后筛选了 28 种 ML 算法;使用准确度、F1 分数和马修斯相关系数 (MCC) 对五个表现最好的方法(即随机森林、标签传播、决策树、标签传播和额外树)进行比较,最后两个适用于不平衡数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 具有完全连接的密集层的 DNN,通过 Adam 优化器的反向传播进行训练,并使用两个和四个隐藏层进行评估。四层网络在损失方面收敛得更快,而跨训练时期的架构之间的准确性没有显着差异。根据提供的测试数据,DNN 的性能优于传统的 ML 模型和其他深度学习方法。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该框架并不特定于一种病原体,因此原则上可以对其进行重新训练,以支持针对其他新出现的传染病的 疫苗 设计。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,所提出的框架可用于设计 猴痘病毒 的多价免疫原,这可以改善 疫苗 的发育和对新兴病毒变体的反应。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于计算机分析,不包括实验验证,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。证据是温和的,因为它基于计算模型并且不涉及直接的生物测试。

title: Early treatment with tecovirimat against mpox disease in cynomolgus macaques
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tecovirimat was developed as an antiviral countermeasure against orthopoxviruses and approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Animal Rule based on efficacy in preclinical studies and clinical pharmacokinetic and safety trials. However, recent randomised clinical trials in patients with mpox who initiated tecovirimat an average of 6-9 days after onset of symptoms did not show improvement in time to resolution of skin lesions. Here, we evaluated whether timing of tecovirimat initiation influenced antiviral efficacy following mpox infection in nonhuman primates and defined the therapeutic window for treatment initiation. METHODS: In this randomised preclinical study, 32 cynomolgus macaques were challenged intravenously with 1 × 106 TCID50 mpox clade IIb virus. Oral tecovirimat (10 mg/kg, once daily for 14 days) treatment was initiated on Day 2 (post-exposure and pre-symptomatic), Day 5 (early symptomatic), or Day 9 (peak symptomatic) after mpox challenge, or no treatment was given as a control group. The primary study endpoint was area under the curve (AUC) and peak numbers of progressive skin lesions. The secondary endpoint was AUC and peak levels of plasma viral loads. Additional analyses included total skin lesions, adaptive immune responses, and transcriptomic signatures. FINDINGS: Treatment adherence was 100%. All tecovirimat-treated animals survived to study completion on Day 28, whereas two untreated control animals required early euthanisation on Days 16 and 17. Tecovirimat efficacy was time-dependent. Progressive skin lesion AUC was significantly lower when treatment was initiated on Day 2 (P 0.99). INTERPRETATION: In this randomised preclinical study, tecovirimat demonstrated antiviral therapeutic efficacy but only when initiated early prior to peak viraemia. These findings emphasise the importance of early initiation of treatment and define the therapeutic window for optimal tecovirimat treatment in nonhuman primates. FUNDING: This study was supported by SIGA Technologies.

title_zh: 早期 治疗 与 特考韦瑞 对抗食蟹猴 猴痘 疾病
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Tecovirimat was developed as an antiviral countermeasure against orthopoxviruses and approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Animal Rule based on efficacy in preclinical studies and clinical pharmacokinetic and safety trials. However, recent randomised clinical trials in patients with mpox who initiated tecovirimat an average of 6-9 days after onset of symptoms did not show improvement in time to resolution of skin lesions. Here, we evaluated whether timing of tecovirimat initiation influenced antiviral efficacy following mpox infection in nonhuman primates and defined the therapeutic window for treatment initiation. METHODS: In this randomised preclinical study, 32 cynomolgus macaques were challenged intravenously with 1 × 106 TCID50 mpox clade IIb virus. Oral tecovirimat (10 mg/kg, once daily for 14 days) treatment was initiated on Day 2 (post-exposure and pre-symptomatic), Day 5 (early symptomatic), or Day 9 (peak symptomatic) after mpox challenge, or no treatment was given as a control group. The primary study endpoint was area under the curve (AUC) and peak numbers of progressive skin lesions. The secondary endpoint was AUC and peak levels of plasma viral loads. Additional analyses included total skin lesions, adaptive immune responses, and transcriptomic signatures. FINDINGS: Treatment adherence was 100%. All tecovirimat-treated animals survived to study completion on Day 28, whereas two untreated control animals required early euthanisation on Days 16 and 17. Tecovirimat efficacy was time-dependent. Progressive skin lesion AUC was significantly lower when treatment was initiated on Day 2 (P 0.99). INTERPRETATION: In this randomised preclinical study, tecovirimat demonstrated antiviral therapeutic efficacy but only when initiated early prior to peak viraemia. These findings emphasise the importance of early initiation of treatment and define the therapeutic window for optimal tecovirimat treatment in nonhuman primates. FUNDING: This study was supported by SIGA Technologies.

title: Severe ocular mpox in an immunocompetent patient
abstract: Mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, is caused by Monkeypox virus (MPXV) and has been associated since 2022 with exanthematous illness in men who have sex with men (MSM), including HIV-negative individuals without prior MPXV vaccination.1,2 The clinical course is usually self-limited, with cutaneous and mucosal involvement.4,10,12 Severe forms, including keratoconjunctivitis and corneal ulcers, are uncommon and have mainly been linked to immunosuppression.2,3,5,10,12,14 We report a 20-year-old MSM male, HIV-negative, immunocompetent, and using pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). He presented with generalized exanthema, right ocular pain, conjunctival injection, tearing, and periorbital cellulitis.1,2,5,10,14 Ophthalmologic evaluation confirmed severe keratoconjunctivitis with progressive corneal ulcers.5-7,10,11,14 MPXV PCR was positive in skin and corneal samples.1,2,10,14 This case highlights the potential for severe ocular disease in a young, otherwise healthy patient and underscores the need for high clinical suspicion, early ophthalmologic assessment, and timely antiviral therapy.2,4,10,15.

source_records.abstract: Mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, is caused by Monkeypox virus (MPXV) and has been associated since 2022 with exanthematous illness in men who have sex with men (MSM), including HIV-negative individuals without prior MPXV vaccination.1,2 The clinical course is usually self-limited, with cutaneous and mucosal involvement.4,10,12 Severe forms, including keratoconjunctivitis and corneal ulcers, are uncommon and have mainly been linked to immunosuppression.2,3,5,10,12,14 We report a 20-year-old MSM male, HIV-negative, immunocompetent, and using pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). He presented with generalized exanthema, right ocular pain, conjunctival injection, tearing, and periorbital cellulitis.1,2,5,10,14 Ophthalmologic evaluation confirmed severe keratoconjunctivitis with progressive corneal ulcers.5-7,10,11,14 MPXV PCR was positive in skin and corneal samples.1,2,10,14 This case highlights the potential for severe ocular disease in a young, otherwise healthy patient and underscores the need for high clinical suspicion, early ophthalmologic assessment, and timely antiviral therapy.2,4,10,15.

title: Clade-specific ophthalmic manifestations of mpox: an umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews.
abstract: BACKGROUND: On 14 August 2024, the WHO redesignated Monkeypox (mpox) as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Ocular disease is under-recognised and can cause irreversible vision loss. Clarifying its burden, clade-specific patterns and HIV-related risks is essential for clinical care and public health. METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review and meta-analysis, systematically searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to September 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews reporting ophthalmic manifestations in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, stratified by viral clades I, II and IIb. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis, with clade-stratified subgroup analyses. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180). RESULTS: Five systematic reviews (36 primary studies; 28 139 patients) were included. The pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.9% (95% CI 4.8 to 13.9), highest in clade I (21.9%) and lowest in clade IIb (2.7%). Keratitis (1.5%), eyelid lesions (3.3%), conjunctival lesions (8.4%) and corneal ulceration (3.3%) varied by clade. Visual impairment occurred in 4.5% overall; unilateral (0.9%) and bilateral (0.4%) blindness were reported only with clade I. Across reviews, people living with advanced HIV experienced disproportionately higher rates of severe and persistent ocular complications than HIV-negative individuals. CONCLUSIONS: Mpox-related ophthalmic disease can cause substantial—and potentially preventable—visual disability. Clade I infection is associated with a greater burden of ocular complications than clade II—particularly IIb. Improved access to eye health services, early recognition and integration of HIV and mpox care are critical to reducing vision loss, especially in resource-limited settings.

analysis.summary_en: This umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews examines the clade-specific ophthalmic manifestations of mpox virus. It identifies significant variations in ocular complications, with clade I showing the highest burden of conjunctivitis and visual impairment, including unilateral and bilateral blindness. The review also highlights the disproportionately higher rates of severe ocular complications in individuals with advanced HIV. These findings underscore the need for improved eye health services and integrated care for mpox and HIV. However, the evidence is limited by heterogeneity, small study numbers, and gaps in understanding the mechanisms and long-term outcomes of ocular complications. The review calls for further research and targeted interventions to address these issues, particularly in resource-limited settings.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 猴痘病毒 的眼科表现,特别检查分支特异性模式以及与 HIV 相关风险的关联。核心问题是确定 猴痘 引起的眼部并发症的负担和特征,重点是 I、II 和 IIb 分支。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是系统综述的总括综述和荟萃分析。从成立到 2025 年 9 月,它系统地检索了 PubMed、Embase、Scopus、Web of Science 和 Cochrane 图书馆。符合条件的研究是报告实验室确诊的 猴痘 病例眼科表现的系统评价,按病毒分支 I、II 和 IIb 分层。使用随机效应荟萃分析和分支分层亚组分析来估计合并比例。该协议已在 PROSPERO 中注册(CRD420251137180)。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 结膜炎的汇总比例为 8.9%(95% CI 4.8 至 13.9),其中 I 型发病率最高(21.9%),IIb 型发病率最低(2.7%)。角膜炎(1.5%)、眼睑病变(3.3%)、结膜病变(8.4%)和角膜溃疡(3.3%)因进化枝而异。总体而言,视力障碍的发生率为 4.5%,单侧(0.9%)和双侧(0.4%)失明仅报告为 I 型。晚期 HIV 感染者的严重和持续性眼部并发症发生率比 HIV 阴性者高得多。猴痘 相关眼科疾病可导致严重且可能可预防的视力障碍。与分支 II 相比,分支 I 感染与眼部并发症的负担更大,尤其是 IIb。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了不同分支和人群所报告的眼部表现的异质性。虽然注意到了进化枝特定的差异,但证据受到研究数量少和报告中潜在偏差的限制。HIV 与眼部并发症之间的关联得到了支持,但需要进一步研究以确认因果关系。缺乏关于长期视力结果和预防眼部并发症的干预措施有效性的数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 改善眼健康服务的可及性、早期识别眼部症状以及将艾滋病毒和 猴痘 护理相结合对于减少视力丧失至关重要,特别是在资源有限的环境中。需要进一步的研究来探索进化枝特异性眼部表现的机制,并评估有针对性的干预措施在预防和管理这些并发症方面的有效性。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 结膜炎的汇总比例为 8.9%(95% CI 4.8 至 13.9),其中 I 型发病率最高(21.9%),IIb 型发病率最低(2.7%)。角膜炎(1.5%)、眼睑病变(3.3%)、结膜病变(8.4%)和角膜溃疡(3.3%)因进化枝而异。总体而言,视力障碍的发生率为 4.5%,单侧(0.9%)和双侧(0.4%)失明仅报告为 I 型。晚期 HIV 感染者的严重和持续性眼部并发症发生率比 HIV 阴性者高得多。猴痘 相关眼科疾病可导致严重且可能可预防的视力障碍。与分支 II 相比,分支 I 感染与眼部并发症的负担更大,尤其是 IIb。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了不同分支和人群所报告的眼部表现的异质性。虽然注意到了进化枝特定的差异,但证据受到研究数量少和报告中潜在偏差的限制。HIV 与眼部并发症之间的关联得到了支持,但需要进一步研究以确认因果关系。缺乏关于长期视力结果和预防眼部并发症的干预措施有效性的数据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 改善眼健康服务的可及性、早期识别眼部症状以及将艾滋病毒和 猴痘 护理相结合对于减少视力丧失至关重要,特别是在资源有限的环境中。需要进一步的研究来探索进化枝特异性眼部表现的机制,并评估有针对性的干预措施在预防和管理这些并发症方面的有效性。

BMJ Journals You are here Home Archive Volume 110, Issue 11 Clade-specific ophthalmic manifestations of mpox: an umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews Email alerts Article Text Article menu Article Text Article info Citation Tools Share Rapid Responses Article metrics Alerts PDF Cornea and ocular surface Clade-specific ophthalmic manifestations of mpox: an umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews Oscar Kallay1, Luxi Ji2, Olalekan A Uthman3, Edward J Mills4, Alimuddin Zumla5,6, Placide Mbala-Kingebeni7, Jean-Jacques Muyembe-Tamfum7, Elie Motulsky8, http://orcid.org/0000-0002-2862-4443Jean B Nachega9,10,11 1 Ophthalmology Department, Centre Médical de l’Alliance, Braine-l’Alleud, Walloon Brabant (Waals-Brabant), Belgium 2 Centre Médical de l’Alliance, Brussels, Braine-I’Alleud, Belgium 3 Division of Health Sciences, Warwick Medical School, Coventry, England, UK 4 Department of Health Research Methods, Evidence and Impact, McMaster University, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada 5 Division of Infection and Immunity, University College London, London, UK 6 University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London, UK 7 National Institute of Biomedical Research, Kinshasa, Congo (Democratic Republic of the) 8 Department of Ophthalmology, Erasmus Hospital, Brussels, Belgium 9 Epidemiology, Infectious Diseases and Microbiology, University of Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA 10 Epidemiology and International Health, Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, Baltimore, Maryland, USA 11 Biomedical Research Institute (BMRI), Stellenbosch University Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences (FMHS), Cape Town, South Africa Correspondence to Dr Jean B Nachega; jbn16{at}pitt.edu Abstract Background On 14 August 2024, the WHO redesignated Monkeypox (mpox) as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Ocular disease is under-recognised and can cause irreversible vision loss. Clarifying its burden, clade-specific patterns and HIV-related risks is essential for clinical care and public health. Methods We conducted an umbrella review and meta-analysis, systematically searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to September 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews reporting ophthalmic manifestations in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, stratified by viral clades I, II and IIb. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis, with clade-stratified subgroup analyses. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180). Results Five systematic reviews (36 primary studies; 28 139 patients) were included. The pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.9% (95% CI 4.8 to 13.9), highest in clade I (21.9%) and lowest in clade IIb (2.7%). Keratitis (1.5%), eyelid lesions (3.3%), conjunctival lesions (8.4%) and corneal ulceration (3.3%) varied by clade. Visual impairment occurred in 4.5% overall; unilateral (0.9%) and bilateral (0.4%) blindness were reported only with clade I. Across reviews, people living with advanced HIV experienced disproportionately higher rates of severe and persistent ocular complications than HIV-negative individuals. Conclusions Mpox-related ophthalmic disease can cause substantial—and potentially preventable—visual disability. Clade I infection is associated with a greater burden of ocular complications than clade II—particularly IIb. Improved access to eye health services, early recognition and integration of HIV and mpox care are critical to reducing vision loss, especially in resource-limited settings. Infection Conjunctiva Cornea Eye (Globe) Vision WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ON THIS TOPIC Ophthalmic complications of Monkeypox (mpox) have been described, but their overall burden, clade-specific differences and interactions with comorbidities, such as HIV, have not been quantified across reviews. WHAT THIS STUDY ADDS To our knowledge, this is the first umbrella review to provide pooled estimates of mpox-related ocular manifestations across 28 139 patients, showing higher proportions in clade I (Ia/Ib) than clade II (IIa/IIb), and greater severity among people with advanced HIV. HOW THIS STUDY MIGHT AFFECT RESEARCH, PRACTICE OR POLICY Findings support enhanced ophthalmic surveillance in clade I-endemic regions, integration of HIV and mpox services to address syndemic risk and incorporation of eye health into outbreak preparedness, vaccination strategies and clinical care pathways. Introduction Monkeypox (mpox) is a zoonotic disease caused by the mpox virus (MPXV), an Orthopoxvirus closely related to the variola virus, which causes smallpox.1 First identified in monkeys in 1958, MPXV was recognised as a human pathogen in 1970 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).2 Two distinct clades have been described: clade I (formerly the Congo Basin clade, subdivided into Ia and Ib) and clade II, further divided into IIa and IIb (formerly the West African clade).3 Clade I is more virulent, with an estimated case fatality ratio (CFR) of 10.6%, compared with 1%–3.6% for clade II.4 The 2022 global outbreak was caused by clade IIb, which had a CFR below 0.2%.5 As of August 2025, WHO data indicate substantial global transmission. In Africa alone, more than 43 000 confirmed cases were reported in the previous 12 months, with the DRC (22 222), Uganda (7979) and Sierra Leone (5245) the most affected; up-to-date figures are available via the WHO Global Mpox Dashboard and situation reports.6–8 Although mpox is primarily known for its cutaneous and systemic features—including fever, rash and lymphadenopathy—it can also affect ocular tissues, leading to substantial morbidity and visual impairment.9 Ocular involvement may result from direct viral invasion or immune-mediated mechanisms, ranging from mild conjunctivitis and blepharitis to keratitis, which can cause corneal scarring and vision loss if untreated, in patients with, or who have had, mpox.10 In severe cases, these complications may culminate in permanent visual disability, with major implications for patients affected, health systems and communities.11 Several systematic reviews have summarised evidence on mpox-related ophthalmic complications. However, no study has quantified the global burden or examined clade-specific and region-specific differences in ocular outcomes. To address this gap, we conducted an umbrella review and meta-analysis to synthesise available data on the proportion of ocular manifestations among mpox cases, with a particular focus on clade-specific variation and the influence of healthcare infrastructure. Methods This umbrella review was conducted according to a protocol prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180) and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines.12 13 Eligibility criteria Defined using the Population-Outcome-Study design (POS) framework: Population: patients of all ages and demographics diagnosed with mpox. Outcome: ophthalmic manifestations and complications, including but not limited to conjunctivitis, blepharitis, keratitis, corneal lesions, impaired vision and blindness. Study design: systematic reviews and meta-analyses of observational studies, case series and case reports. Only systematic reviews published in English were included. No restrictions were placed on publication date or geography. Where a review used a systematic search but did not fulfil all criteria for a systematic review, this was noted during data extraction. Information sources and search strategy We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to 11 September 2025. The strategy, developed with an information specialist, combined keywords and Medical Subject Headings related to mpox, ophthalmic manifestations and systematic reviews. The full search strategies are provided in the online supplemental material (annex 1). Supplemental material [bjo-2025-328294supp001.pdf] Study selection Two independent reviewers screened all records in Covidence (Veritas Health Innovation, Melbourne, Australia) in two stages: (1) title/abstract and (2) full text against eligibility criteria. Disagreements were resolved by discussion or adjudication by a third reviewer. Data collection and items A standardised extraction form was piloted. Two reviewers independently extracted study characteristics, mpox clade, ophthalmic manifestations, proportions of ocular outcomes among mpox cases and any reported clade-specific or geographic differences. Discrepancies were resolved by consensus or input from a third reviewer. Data were managed in Microsoft Excel. Clade classification methodology Because many included studies did not specify the MPXV clade, we inferred the clade based on geographic location, study period and epidemiological context: Clade I (Central African clade; Ia and Ib): studies from the DRC, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo and Sudan. Although Cameroon has historically reported both clades I and II, no Cameroon-specific ocular studies met the inclusion criteria; therefore, Cameroon was not used to assign a clade in pooled analyses. Clade II (West African clade; IIa and IIb): studies from Nigeria and other West African countries primarily correspond to IIa. Subtype IIb was assumed for post2022 studies conducted in non-endemic settings, aligning with the multicountry outbreak beginning in 2022. Risk of bias assessment We appraised the methodological quality of included reviews using AMSTAR 2 (A MeaSurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews).14 Two reviewers assessed each study independently; discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Synthesis of results We calculated pooled proportions of ocular manifestations using random-effects meta-analysis (Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation). Subgroup analyses were conducted by clade. Given high heterogeneity (I2>50% in several analyses), we also reported 95% prediction intervals to reflect between-study variability. Terminology ‘Proportion’ refers to the frequency (%) of ocular manifestations among mpox cases in the included studies. Where no timeframe was specified, estimates represent proportion at presentation or during follow-up. Results Characteristics of the included reviews Searches identified 71 records (online supplemental figure 1: PRISMA flow diagram). After removing 23 duplicates, 48 titles/abstracts were screened; 9 full texts were assessed, and 4 were excluded as narrative reviews, leaving 5 eligible systematic reviews (2023–2025; online supplemental table 1). These synthesised 5–25 observational studies each (published 1980–2024). Primary study quality ranged from poor to high, with most studies rated as moderate to high. Risk of bias assessment AMSTAR 2 ratings are reported in online supplemental table 2.14 All five systematic reviews were rated as high quality, indicating generally robust methodology. Sample characteristics of included primary studies 36 studies reporting ocular manifestations in 28 139 patients with mpox were analysed (online supplemental table 3). The studies demonstrated substantial geographic diversity, with data from the USA (n=8), DRC (n=9), Nigeria (n=4), Mexico (n=3), Brazil (n=2), UK (n=2), Spain (n=1), France (n=1), Portugal (n=1), Canada (n=1), Saudi Arabia (n=1), Sudan (n=1), Republic of the Congo (n=1) and multi-country studies (n=2). 23 studies (2022–2024) predominantly represented clade IIb infections from non-endemic regions, while 13 earlier studies documented endemic African outbreaks associated with clade I (n=10) and clade IIa (n=3). No Cameroon-specific ocular studies were identified despite its unique epidemiological position reporting both clades. Several studies highlighted a disproportionate burden of severe and persistent ocular complications among people living with advanced HIV, particularly in clade I settings.15 16 Ophthalmic manifestations by MPXV clade Conjunctivitis by clade Across 25 studies, including 27 022 patients, the pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.86% (95% CI 4.84 to 13.85; prediction interval 0.00% to 43.49%) (figure 1). Clade-specific estimates differed: clade I 21.86% (95% CI 14.74 to 29.87; prediction interval 3.31% to 49.31%; I2=82%), clade IIa 16.91% (95% CI 12.54 to 21.74; prediction interval 9.18%–26.26%) and clade IIb 2.74% (95% CI 0.79 to 5.70; prediction interval 0.00% to 20.86%; I2=97.6%). Wide prediction intervals reflect expected variability across settings and study designs. Download figure Open in new tab Download powerpoint Figure 1 Pooled proportion of conjunctivitis by clade type. Keratitis by clade From eight studies (1957 patients), the pooled proportion of keratitis was 1.53% (95% CI 0.75 to 2.55; prediction interval 0.00% to 4.92%) (figure 2). Estimates were higher in clade I at 2.88% (95% CI 1.43 to 4.77; prediction interval 0.00% to 11.29%) than in clade IIa at 0.82% (95% CI 0.31 to 1.51; prediction interval 0.16% to 1.84%). Download figure Open in new tab Download powerpoint Figure 2 Pooled proportion of keratitis by clade type. Eyelid lesions by clade Across six studies (816 patients), the pooled proportion of eyelid lesions was 3.25% (95% CI 0.26 to 8.61; prediction interval 0.00% to 27.74%) (figure 3). Clade-specific evidence was limited: clade I 4.26% (95% CI 0.83 to 14.85; single study) and clade IIb 1.11% (95% CI 0.00 to 3.45; single study). An overall pooled estimate labelled ‘clade II’ at 3.94% (95% CI 0.00 to 13.47; prediction interval 0.00% to 52.38%) reflects mixed or unspecified II subtypes; interpret with caution. Download figure Open in new tab Download powerpoint Figure 3 Pooled proportion of eyelid lesions by clade type. Conjunctival lesions by clade Across three studies (601 patients), the pooled proportion was 8.37% (95% CI 1.81 to 18.64; prediction interval 0.00% to 64.12%) (figure 4). Clade I was 11.61% (95% CI 2.99 to 24.70; prediction interval 0.00% to 100.00%; I2=93.8%; two studies), while clade II (single study) was 2.13% (95% CI 0.58 to 11.97). Download figure Open in new tab Download powerpoint Figure 4 Pooled proportion of conjunctival lesions by clade type. Corneal ulceration by clade Across three studies (654 patients), the pooled proportion was 3.33% (95% CI 1.99 to 4.95; prediction interval 0.77–7.23%) (figure 5). Clade I was 3.69% (95% CI 2.32 to 5.35; prediction interval 0.00–18.99%; I2=0%) with consistent rates between studies (3.25% and 4.26%), and clade II (single study) was 2.94% (95% CI 0.85 to 16.19). Download figure Open in new tab Download powerpoint Figure 5 Pooled proportion of corneal ulceration by clade type. Visual impairment and blindness by clade Across five studies (986 patients; online supplemental figure 2), the pooled proportion of impaired vision was 4.48% (95% CI 1.30 to 9.21; prediction interval 0.00% to 24.37%). Clade-specific rates varied: clade I 4.20% (95% CI 1.16 to 8.88; prediction interval 0.00% to 32.30%; I2=87.8%), clade II 14.00% (95% CI 6.23 to 26.96; single study) and clade IIb 1.00% (95% CI 0.00 to 5.03; single study). Pooled unilateral blindness from two studies (329 patients; online supplemental figure 3) was 0.90% (95% CI 0.04 to 2.46; prediction interval 0.00% to 20.16%), both in clade I. Bilateral blindness (one clade I study; 282 patients; online supplemental figure 4) was 0.35% (95% CI 0.01 to 1.96). Subgroup analyses and case reports indicate more severe, less responsive ocular disease among people with advanced HIV, including prolonged keratitis and vision loss.15 16 Discussion This umbrella review and meta-analysis assesses the proportion of mpox-related ophthalmic manifestations, with emphasis on variation by viral clade. title: SARS, H1N1, EBOLA, COVID-19, MPOX, H5N1 AND HANTAVIRUS: IS HUMANITY ENTERING A NEW ERA OF PANDEMIC? IS TÜRKİYE PREPARED FOR THE NEXT GLOBAL OUTBREAK?
abstract: The emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases pose persistent challenges to global health security. Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.
journal: International Journal of Health Services Research and Policy

Outbreaks such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections highlight the need for effective preparedness against emerging infectious threats. The concept of “Disease X” further emphasizes the importance of preparing for unknown pathogens that may cause future epidemics or pandemics. This study aimed to examine major infectious disease outbreaks and assess Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future global outbreaks. A descriptive review design was employed, based on a structured literature search and document analysis of scientific publications and institutional reports. The findings were organized and interpreted using a SWOT framework. The analysis identified healthcare infrastructure, intensive care capacity, digital health systems, and experience gained during the COVID-19 pandemic as potential strengths. However, challenges related to healthcare workforce capacity, zoonotic disease surveillance, public health literacy, coordination across human, animal, and environmental health sectors, and dependence on external sources for certain biotechnological products may constrain preparedness. Climate change, environmental disruption, international travel, migration, and global trade were identified as factors that may influence the emergence and spread of infectious diseases. Strengthening integrated surveillance and early warning systems, improving intersectoral coordination through the One Health approach, enhancing domestic vaccine and diagnostic production capacity, and expanding community-based public health education may help improve Türkiye’s preparedness for future outbreaks. These findings highlight the importance of sustained, multisectoral preparedness for emerging infectious disease threats.
source_records.journal: International Journal of Health Services Research and Policy

abstract_zh: 传染病的出现和再次出现对全球卫生安全构成持续挑战。暴发,例如严重急性呼吸系统综合症 (SARS)、甲型流感 (H1N1)、埃博拉病毒病、2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19)、猴痘、甲型禽流感 (H5N1) 和汉坦病毒感染,凸显了针对新出现的传染病威胁做好有效准备的必要性。“X疾病”的概念进一步强调了为可能导致未来流行病或大流行的未知病原体做好准备的重要性。本研究旨在检查主要传染病 暴发 并评估土耳其对未来潜在的全球 暴发 的准备情况。基于对科学出版物和机构报告的结构化文献检索和文档分析,采用了描述性综述设计。使用 SWOT 框架对调查结果进行组织和解释。该分析将医疗基础设施、重症监护能力、数字医疗系统以及在 COVID-19 大流行期间获得的经验确定为潜在优势。然而,与医疗保健劳动力能力、人畜共患疾病、公共卫生素养、人类、动物和环境卫生部门之间的协调以及某些生物技术产品对外部来源的依赖相关的挑战可能会限制准备工作。气候变化、环境破坏、国际旅行、移民和全球贸易被认为是可能影响传染病出现和传播的因素。加强综合 监测 和早期预警系统,通过“同一个健康”方法改善部门间协调,提高国内 疫苗 和诊断生产能力,以及扩大基于社区的公共卫生教育,可能有助于改善土耳其对未来 暴发 的准备。这些发现凸显了针对新出现的传染病威胁进行持续、多部门准备的重要性。

title: SPR Analysis of Monkeypox Proteins A29L and E8L Glycan Interaction and Inhibition by Marine-Derived Glycans
abstract: The global resurgence of mpox has established monkeypox virus (MPXV), comprising Clades I and II, as a significant public health threat. Studies of homologous vaccinia virus proteins indicate that cell-surface glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), including heparan sulfate (HS) and chondroitin sulfate (CS), facilitate viral attachment and entry. However, direct interactions between GAGs and MPXV surface proteins A29L/E8L remain poorly characterized. Using surface plasmon resonance (SPR), we quantified the apparent binding affinities of A29L (Clade I KD = 0.8 ± 0.3 nM) and E8L (Clade I KD = 1.2 ± 0.2 nM; Clade II KD = 1.6 ± 0.1 nM) for heparin, a common HS analog. We also quantified E8L apparent binding affinities to CS-A (Clade I KD = 0.4 ± 0.2 nM; Clade II KD = 0.65 ± 0.06 nM) and CS-E (KD = 0.6 ± 0.1 nM; Clade II KD = 0.70 ± 0.08 nM). We further determined that Clade I A29L and E8L preferentially recognized long-chain fully sulfated or N-sulfated heparin. Lastly, we determined a small library of marine-derived sulfated glycans (MSGs) as effective inhibitors for the Clade I E8L and A29L protein-GAG interface. These findings establish previously uncharacterized binding interactions and identify MSGs as potential candidates for anti-mpox drug development.

However, direct interactions between GAGs and MPXV surface proteins A29L/E8L remain poorly characterized. Using surface plasmon resonance (SPR), we quantified the apparent binding affinities of A29L (Clade I KD = 0.8 ± 0.3 nM) and E8L (Clade I KD = 1.2 ± 0.2 nM; Clade II KD = 1.6 ± 0.1 nM) for heparin, a common HS analog. We also quantified E8L apparent binding affinities to CS-A (Clade I KD = 0.4 ± 0.2 nM; Clade II KD = 0.65 ± 0.06 nM) and CS-E (KD = 0.6 ± 0.1 nM; Clade II KD = 0.70 ± 0.08 nM). We further determined that Clade I A29L and E8L preferentially recognized long-chain fully sulfated or N-sulfated heparin. Lastly, we determined a small library of marine-derived sulfated glycans (MSGs) as effective inhibitors for the Clade I E8L and A29L protein-GAG interface. These findings establish previously uncharacterized binding interactions and identify MSGs as potential candidates for anti-mpox drug development.

abstract_zh: 猴痘 在全球范围内的卷土重来已确定由 I 型和 II 型分支组成的猴痘病毒 (MPXV) 已成为重大的公共卫生威胁。对同源痘苗病毒蛋白的研究表明,细胞表面糖胺聚糖 (GAG),包括硫酸乙酰肝素 (HS) 和硫酸软骨素 (CS),可促进病毒附着和进入。然而,GAG 和 MPXV 表面蛋白 A29L/E8L 之间的直接相互作用仍知之甚少。使用表面等离子共振 (SPR),我们量化了 A29L(Clade I KD = 0.8 ± 0.3 nM)和 E8L(Clade I KD = 1.2 ± 0.2 nM;Clade II KD = 1.6 ± 0.1 nM)对常见 HS 类似物肝素的表观结合亲和力。我们还量化了 E8L 与 CS-A(进化枝 I KD = 0.4 ± 0.2 nM;进化枝 II KD = 0.65 ± 0.06 nM)和 CS-E(KD = 0.6 ± 0.1 nM;进化枝 II KD = 0.70 ± 0.08 nM)的表观结合亲和力。我们进一步确定,Clade I A29L 和 E8L 优先识别长链完全硫酸化或 N-硫酸化肝素。最后,我们确定了一个小型海洋源性硫酸聚糖 (MSG) 文库作为 Clade I E8L 和 A29L 蛋白-GAG 界面的有效抑制剂。这些发现建立了以前未表征的结合相互作用,并将 MSG 确定为抗 猴痘 药物开发的潜在候选者。

title: Single-Step Sample-Activated Alternating Sequential Flow Enables Autonomous Multistep Electrochemical Lateral Flow Detection of Mpox Virus DNA
abstract: Abstract The 2022 multinational mpox virus (MPXV) outbreak and continued cross-border transmission have highlighted limitations of laboratory-confined PCR diagnostics. Here, we report an alternating lateral flow architecture (ALFA) that transforms traditional single-pass lateral flow into a programmable platform for autonomous multistep electrochemical nucleic acid detection following a single prepared-sample introduction. By regulating passive fluid delivery, ALFA enables sequential molecular processing and in situ signal generation without external intervention. Coupled with Ag(I)-mediated mismatch DNA nanocomplexes (MDNs), the system provides electrochemical signal amplification without nucleic acid amplification. ALFA detected MPXV DNA with a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.55 pM and a linear range of 101−105 pM. In urine and saliva spiked with structurally intact viral particles, the lowest statistically distinguishable concentration was 10 copies mL−1. Clinical evaluation of 50 PCR-characterized lesion swab samples yielded 92.11% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and 94.0% accuracy. The platform also maintained stable performance over an estimated 112 days. ALFA therefore provides a programmable lateral flow framework for rapid, amplification-free, decentralized nucleic acid diagnostics.

title: Identification of Mpox Skin Lesion Images Based on Deep Learning Classification Models
abstract: Mpox (formerly known as monkeypox) is a rare zoonotic disease that can cause skin lesions and has the potential for global spread. With the deepening integration of computer science and medicine, intelligent disease detection models based on deep learning and neural networks have become important auxiliary tools for enhancing clinical diagnosis and treatment. This study conducted a comparative analysis of the performance of mainstream deep learning classification models,VGG19, ResNet50, DenseNet201, GoogLeNet, and ConvNeXt_B,in the task of mpox skin image recognition. For the binary classification task, images were categorized into a “Mpox” class and an “Others” class, where the latter includes chickenpox and measles cases, given that their initial rash and pustule presentations closely resemble those of mpox. Beyond quantitative performance evaluation, this study further employed GradCAM++ to generate class activation heatmaps, providing visual interpretability of model decision-making. The resulting heatmaps offer critical clinical diagnostic value by highlighting key lesion regions, thereby enhancing model transparency and supporting clinicians in validating predictions. The experimental results indicate that under identical model parameters and learning rates, the ResNet50 model achieved higher classification accuracy and inference speed, demonstrating its application potential for accurate diagnosis in mpox and other disease image recognition tasks.
journal: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence

title: HECA-YOLOv11: A High-Accuracy Hybrid Attention Network for Real-Time Monkeypox Skin Lesion Detection with Interpretability
abstract: Introduction: The global outbreak risk of monkeypox necessitates efficient diagnostic tools. Current methods are slow and struggle to differentiate similar skin lesions, while deep learning models lack both accuracy and interpretability for multi-class classification. This study aims to develop a high-performance, real-time screening tool for early detection of monkeypox and similar conditions. Methods: This study proposes an enhanced architecture that incorporates the Highly Efficient Channel Attention (HECA) mechanism into YOLOv11 to improve feature selection. HECA performs Global Average Pooling (GAP) and Max Average Pooling (MAP) on input feature maps. Using spatial transformations and pixel-domain enhancements, the research establishes and augments a four-class dataset containing monkeypox, measles, chickenpox, and normal skin images. Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) generates heatmaps for lesion localization visualization, while a PyQt5-based interactive diagnostic interface streamlines clinical workflows. Results: Experimental results demonstrate the proposed model’s superior performance compared to existing approaches (EfficientNet-v2-l, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, VGG19, MobileNetv2, DenseNet201, and YOLOv11s) on the test set, with enhanced detection speed, accuracy (98.9%), precision (99%), recall (99.3%), and F1-score (99.1%). HECA-YOLOv11 outperforms SE-YOLOv11 and ECA-YOLOv11 by over 5.1% across all evaluation metrics. Heatmap analysis confirms the model’s focus on lesion regions, aligning with medical reasoning. Discussion: The integrated attention mechanism and interpretability techniques effectively address key limitations in automated skin lesion detection. The high performance and low latency signify a major advancement towards reliable clinical decision support, with important implications for early outbreak containment. Conclusion: The HECA-YOLOv11 framework provides a highly accurate and efficient tool for early monkeypox screening. Its standardized interface holds significant potential to accelerate public health responses and improve global control of emerging infectious diseases.

title: Healthcare Workers’ Preparedness for Monkeypox Pandemic Response in SubSaharan Africa: A Rapid Review Investigating the Knowledge Gap
abstract: Background: Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease caused by an Orthopoxvirus endemic to sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where its resurgence underscores the urgent need for improved preparedness among health care workers (HCWs). Despite the potential of a One Health approach, current implementations remain fragmented. This rapid review synthesises evidence on HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, information sources, and barriers to preparedness regarding Mpox in SSA to identify training needs and policy implications. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched using MeSH terms and Boolean operators for studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies assessing HCW knowledge, attitudes, or preparedness for Mpox in SSA with full-text availability in English or French were included; those involving non-HCW populations, conducted outside SSA, or lacking primary data were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardised template; quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical CrossSectional Studies. Results: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels. Conclusion: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.
journal: Journal of Clinical Virology and Translational Research

title: Synthesis and Structure−Activity Relationship (SAR) of Hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamides against Orthopoxviruses
abstract: Abstract We have previously identified hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a as a potent antiviral hit against vaccinia virus (VACV) and monkeypox virus (MPXV), albeit with extremely low solubility. Herein, we have conducted antiviral structure−activity relationship (SAR)-directed and solubility-driven synthesis of a total of 57 analogs. In the primary VACV reporter assay, many analogs demonstrated nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral potency without significant cytotoxicity, with analog 4m showing 10-fold improved potency. Plaque assays against VACV and MPXV confirmed the strong antiviral activities. We also discovered that amide N-methylation drastically enhanced solubility via disrupting an intramolecular H-bond. Specifically, we identified an N-methylated analog (4f) with >1000-fold improved solubility while retaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM). In addition, compound 4f exhibited dose−response potency against MPXV in the plaque assay and highly favorable ADME properties. Overall, our current work characterizes 4f as a strong antiviral lead and solidifies amide N-methylation as a viable approach toward further lead development.

title_zh: 羟基吡啶酮-3-甲酰胺的合成及针对 正痘病毒 的构效关系 (SAR)
source_body_en: Abstract We have previously identified hydroxypyridone-3-carboxamide 4a as a potent antiviral hit against vaccinia virus (VACV) and monkeypox virus (MPXV), albeit with extremely low solubility. Herein, we have conducted antiviral structure−activity relationship (SAR)-directed and solubility-driven synthesis of a total of 57 analogs. In the primary VACV reporter assay, many analogs demonstrated nanomolar to sub-micromolar antiviral potency without significant cytotoxicity, with analog 4m showing 10-fold improved potency. Plaque assays against VACV and MPXV confirmed the strong antiviral activities. We also discovered that amide N-methylation drastically enhanced solubility via disrupting an intramolecular H-bond. Specifically, we identified an N-methylated analog (4f) with >1000-fold improved solubility while retaining potency (EC50 = 0.69 μM). In addition, compound 4f exhibited dose−response potency against MPXV in the plaque assay and highly favorable ADME properties. Overall, our current work characterizes 4f as a strong antiviral lead and solidifies amide N-methylation as a viable approach toward further lead development.

title: Probe-Free, Primer-Programmed Amplicon Encoding Enables Nanopore-Based Multiplex Detection With Deep Learning Decoding.
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐reaction multiplex nucleic acid testing (NATs) must both co‐amplify multiple targets and distinguish the resulting amplicons within the product mixture. Most conventional assays achieve this distinction using target‐specific reporters or other external encoding elements. Here, we introduce a primer‐programmed multiplexing strategy in which primer design generates target‐associated amplicons with predefined lengths that are read electrically with nanopores. In a proof‐of‐concept implementation, one‐pot recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) generated four amplicons with predefined product lengths from Monkeypox (Mpox), Cowpox, Vaccinia, and human RNase P. The resulting amplicons were analyzed with glass nanopores, and individual translocation events were classified by a deep neural network (DNN) based on a six‐dimensional feature set derived from nanopore recordings. Event‐level decoding achieved >95% accuracy, >94.7% sensitivity, and >98.3% specificity, and aggregation of classified events yielded sample‐level calls with >93.3% sensitivity and >93.9% specificity in blinded samples, with qualitative calls matching polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results across the 9 PCR‐benchmarked samples. These results demonstrate a probe‐free multiplexing architecture in which target identity is programmed through primer‐defined amplicon design and decoded from the resulting multidimensional nanopore response using a DNN, eliminating the need for target‐specific reporter chemistry and opening new opportunities for all‐electrical multiplex nucleic acid testing based on unmodified amplification products.

title_zh: 无探针、引物编程的扩增子编码可通过深度学习解码实现基于纳米孔的多重检测。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Single‐reaction multiplex nucleic acid testing (NATs) must both co‐amplify multiple targets and distinguish the resulting amplicons within the product mixture. Most conventional assays achieve this distinction using target‐specific reporters or other external encoding elements. Here, we introduce a primer‐programmed multiplexing strategy in which primer design generates target‐associated amplicons with predefined lengths that are read electrically with nanopores. In a proof‐of‐concept implementation, one‐pot recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) generated four amplicons with predefined product lengths from Monkeypox (Mpox), Cowpox, Vaccinia, and human RNase P. The resulting amplicons were analyzed with glass nanopores, and individual translocation events were classified by a deep neural network (DNN) based on a six‐dimensional feature set derived from nanopore recordings. Event‐level decoding achieved >95% accuracy, >94.7% sensitivity, and >98.3% specificity, and aggregation of classified events yielded sample‐level calls with >93.3% sensitivity and >93.9% specificity in blinded samples, with qualitative calls matching polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results across the 9 PCR‐benchmarked samples. These results demonstrate a probe‐free multiplexing architecture in which target identity is programmed through primer‐defined amplicon design and decoded from the resulting multidimensional nanopore response using a DNN, eliminating the need for target‐specific reporter chemistry and opening new opportunities for all‐electrical multiplex nucleic acid testing based on unmodified amplification products.
abstract_zh: 摘要 单反应多重核酸检测 (NAT) 必须同时扩增多个靶标并区分产物混合物中产生的扩增子。大多数传统测定使用目标特异性报告基因或其他外部编码元件来实现这种区别。在这里,我们引入了一种引物编程的多重策略,其中引物设计生成具有预定义长度的目标相关扩增子,这些扩增子可以通过纳米孔进行电读取。在概念验证实施中,一锅重组酶聚合酶扩增 (RPA) 生成了来自猴痘 (猴痘)、牛痘、牛痘和人 RNase P 的四个具有预定义产物长度的扩增子。使用玻璃纳米孔分析所得扩增子,并通过基于纳米孔记录衍生的六维特征集的深度神经网络 (DNN) 对各个易位事件进行分类。事件级解码实现了 >95% 的准确度、>94.7% 的灵敏度和 >98.3% 的特异性,分类事件的聚合在盲样样本中产生了 >93.3% 的灵敏度和 >93.9% 的特异性的样本级判别,定性判别与 9 个 PCR 基准样本中的聚合酶链式反应 (PCR) 结果相匹配。这些结果展示了一种无探针多重架构,其中目标身份通过引物定义的扩增子设计进行编程,并使用 DNN 从生成的多维纳米孔响应中进行解码,消除了对目标特异性报告化学的需要,并为基于未修饰的扩增产物的全电多重核酸测试开辟了新的机会。

title: Reassessing the diversity and distribution of African rope squirrels ( Funisciurus Trouessart, 1880) in the Congo Basin
abstract: Abstract The taxonomy, distribution, and ecology of sub-Saharan squirrels are poorly documented. This study focuses on the diversity and distribution of rope squirrels (Funisciurus Trouessart, 1880) in the Congo Basin. We compiled the most comprehensive genetic (n = 397 sequences) and morphometric (n = 219 measured skulls) dataset to date, covering much of their geographical and taxonomic range. Analysis of mitochondrial markers recovered 10 MOTUs (Molecular Operational Taxonomic Unit), nuclear markers 2 MOTUs, and morphometrics 5 Operational Taxonomic Units. Integrating this evidence suggests at least six species-level lineages in our dataset: four allopatric taxa related to F. anerythrus; four genetically different taxa (of which two are sympatric species) that resemble F. bayonii; one taxon corresponding to F. pyrropus akka de Winton, 1895; one morphologically distinct taxon that resembles F. congicus; and one unidentified taxon. Their distributional ranges reveal that the Congo and Kasaï Rivers act as major biogeographical barriers, suggesting that they originated by allopatric speciation. Our findings provide a baseline for studying the effects of habitat loss on rope squirrel populations in the Congo Basin and inform research into their role as reservoirs of zoonotic pathogens, including mpox virus.

title: A validated, high-throughput and resource-efficient digital densitometric method for antiviral and cytotoxicity screening against poxviruses
abstract: Reference methods in antiviral drug discovery, the plaque reduction assay (PRA) and viral yield reduction, are labor-intensive and low-throughput, whereas tetrazolium-based metabolic assays (MTT) may be unsuitable for viruses that sustain host-cell metabolism during productive infection, including poxviruses. We validated a digital densitometric assay (DDA), which quantifies antiviral and cytotoxic effects in crystal violet-stained monolayers using the open-source software Fiji/ImageJ, against three reference methods, with vaccinia virus strain Western Reserve in Vero cells. Across 38 fungal extracts, DDA agreed substantially with PRA for antiviral activity (Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, CCC = 0.869; 95% limits of agreement -31.5 to +21.1 percentage points) and moderately with MTT for cytotoxicity (CCC = 0.677) and was more precise between replicates (median coefficient of variation 2.5% versus 5.5%). For the test compound FAC22, the half-maximal cytotoxic concentration was 238.3 μM by DDA and 46.4 μM by MTT, a five-fold difference between readouts; the half-maximal effective concentration was 8.83 μM by viral yield reduction and 11.9 μM by DDA over its non-cytotoxic range. In infected cultures MTT separated virus and cell controls by only 1.08 to 1.39-fold, precluding estimation of an effective concentration, against 1.8 to 2.3-fold for DDA. DDA met conventional robustness criteria on the screening plate (Z' = 0.818 antiviral, 0.861 cytotoxicity), comparable to PRA (Z' = 0.91), cut reagent consumption by 80 to 90%, and shortened analysis from 20 min to under 1 min per plate. DDA is accurate, resource-efficient and scalable for poxvirus screening, and applicable to other cytopathic viruses pending validation.

We validated a digital densitometric assay (DDA), which quantifies antiviral and cytotoxic effects in crystal violet-stained monolayers using the open-source software Fiji/ImageJ, against three reference methods, with vaccinia virus strain Western Reserve in Vero cells. Across 38 fungal extracts, DDA agreed substantially with PRA for antiviral activity (Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, CCC = 0.869; 95% limits of agreement -31.5 to +21.1 percentage points) and moderately with MTT for cytotoxicity (CCC = 0.677) and was more precise between replicates (median coefficient of variation 2.5% versus 5.5%). For the test compound FAC22, the half-maximal cytotoxic concentration was 238.3 μM by DDA and 46.4 μM by MTT, a five-fold difference between readouts; the half-maximal effective concentration was 8.83 μM by viral yield reduction and 11.9 μM by DDA over its non-cytotoxic range. In infected cultures MTT separated virus and cell controls by only 1.08 to 1.39-fold, precluding estimation of an effective concentration, against 1.8 to 2.3-fold for DDA. DDA met conventional robustness criteria on the screening plate (Z' = 0.818 antiviral, 0.861 cytotoxicity), comparable to PRA (Z' = 0.91), cut reagent consumption by 80 to 90%, and shortened analysis from 20 min to under 1 min per plate. DDA is accurate, resource-efficient and scalable for poxvirus screening, and applicable to other cytopathic viruses pending validation.

full_text: AbstractObjective To analyze adherence to health vulnerability behaviors among men who have sex with men during the mpox public health emergency in Brazil. Method A cross-sectional, analytical study conducted in a virtual environment between September and December 2022 via an electronic questionnaire, with recruitment via social media/dating apps. The outcome of interest comprised four variables related to health vulnerability behaviors, and a multivariable analysis was conducted using a generalized linear model. Results A total of 1,449 men who reported having sex with men participated in the study, with a prevalence of health vulnerability behaviors of 13.9% (n=202), mainly due to not being vaccinated against mpox (50.4%), not adopting preventive care measures (30.6%), not undergoing testing (26.2%), and not following health treatment (9.9%). The multivariable model indicated a higher prevalence of the outcome independently associated with intimate contact with a person with mpox (adjusted prevalence ratio [APR]: 1.82; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 1.33; 2.48), non-disclosure of serological status (APR 1.40; 95%CI 1.05; 1.87), and disbelief in mpox-related homophobia (APR 1.39; 95%CI 1.01; 1.90). The use of glory holes was associated with a lower prevalence (APR 0.43; 95%CI 0.20; 0.92). Conclusion Greater health vulnerability was identified among participants who exhibited behaviors associated with a higher risk of mpox exposure, highlighting the need to plan targeted, population-based actions.Keywords: Sexual Vulnerability; Risk-Taking; Men’s Health; Mpox, Monkeypox; Cross-Sectional Studies ResumoObjetivo Analisar a adesão a comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde entre homens que fazem sexo com homens na emergência de saúde pública de mpox no Brasil. Método Estudo transversal, analítico, realizado em ambiente virtual entre setembro e dezembro de 2022 via questionário eletrônico, com recrutamento em redes sociais/aplicativos de relacionamento. O desfecho de interesse do estudo foi composto por quatro variáveis de comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde e foi aplicada regressão multivariada dos dados pelo modelo de regressão linear generalizado. Resultados Participaram do estudo 1.449 homens que afirmaram fazer sexo com homens, uma prevalência de comportamentos de vulnerabilidade à saúde de 13,9% (n=202), principalmente por não se vacinarem contra a mpox (50,4%), não adotarem medidas de cuidado (30,6%), não realizarem testagem (26,2%) e não seguirem tratamento de saúde (9,9%). O modelo multivariado indicou maior prevalência do desfecho associada independentemente a contato íntimo com pessoa com mpox (razões de prevalência ajustada [RP ajustada]: 1,82; intervalos de confiança de 95% [IC95%] 1,33; 2,48), a não revelação do status sorológico (RP ajustada 1,40; IC95% 1,05; 1,87) e à descrença em homofobia relacionada à mpox (RP ajustada 1,39; IC95% 1,01; 1,90). O uso de glory holes (buracos da glória) associou-se à menor prevalência (RP ajustada 0,43; IC95% 0,20; 0,92). Conclusão Identificou-se maior vulnerabilidade à saúde entre participantes que apresentaram comportamentos relacionados ao maior risco de exposição ao mpox, o que enseja planejamento de ações populacionais específicas.Palavras-chave: Vulnerabilidade Sexual, Assunção de Riscos, Saúde do Homem, Mpox, Estudos Transversais MethodsStudy designThis is a cross-sectional, analytical, and quantitative study conducted via a web survey, that is, an electronic questionnaire applied exclusively in a virtual environment. This manuscript followed the recommendations of the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE).SettingData collection took place between September and December 2022, a period that coincided with the mpox outbreak in Brazil, during which reported cases were more concentrated in the states of São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro [15]. Participants were recruited exclusively in a virtual environment, through digital social networks (Facebook, Instagram, X), instant messaging applications (WhatsApp and Telegram), and dating and sexual networking applications (Hornet, Grindr, Scruff, and Tinder), all with a recognized queer and/or gay perspective. To enable participation, a specific research profile was created on these platforms, including a study description with a link to access the electronic questionnaire.ParticipantsThe study population consisted of Brazilian men who used social networks and interaction applications. Inclusion criteria were: self-identifying as a man (cisgender or transgender); having had at least one sexual encounter with another man in the past 12 months; being 18 years of age or older; and residing in Brazil. Individuals who were outside the country during the data collection period were excluded from the analysis. Identification and recruitment of participants were conducted online through the dissemination of the research profile on social networks, instant messaging applications, and dating applications.Data sources and measurementData collection was carried out via an electronic questionnaire hosted on the REDCap platform. The instrument, validated (face and content) by five experts and five participants, consisted of 46 questions distributed across four sections: (a) sociodemographic information; (b) sexual-affective relationships; (c) sexual behaviors and practices; (d) use of health services, experiences, proximity, and perceptions regarding stigma/fear related to mpox.Recruitment combined two strategies. First, the virtual snowball sampling technique [16] was used, in which 20 men who have sex with men, selected as “seeds” (diverse in terms of region, race/skin color, income, and education), were invited to share the research link within their networks. Second, direct dissemination was carried out through profiles created for the study on social networks (Facebook, Instagram, X), messaging applications (WhatsApp, Telegram), and dating applications (Hornet, Grindr, Scruff, and Tinder).VariablesThe study outcome was a dichotomous variable (yes/no) composed of four behaviors: (1) would follow mpox treatment if diagnosed; (2) would undergo mpox testing if a testing center were available; (3) would receive vaccination against mpox, if the vaccine was available; (4) would take measures for self-care and notify contacts if diagnosed. If a participant responded “no” to at least one of the aforementioned variables, they were classified as “adherent to at least one health vulnerability behavior,” defined as at least one negative response regarding testing, treatment, vaccination, or contact notification related to mpox.These behaviors were presented in the results of this manuscript, all measured dichotomously (yes/no): “Presented at least one vulnerability behavior”; “Presented two or more vulnerability behaviors”; “Would not be vaccinated against mpox”; “Would not take self-care/contact notification measures”; “Would not undergo mpox testing”; and “Would not follow treatment if diagnosed”. The first two variables were used exclusively for sample description.Independent variables comprised three main dimensions:Sociodemographic: being a young adult (<30 years) (yes/no); gender identity (cis/trans); homosexual orientation (yes/no); marital status (without a partner/with a partner); race/skin color (White/Non-White, including Black, Brown [Brazilian mixed race], Asian, and Indigenous, grouped according to recommendations [17]); having a religion (yes/no); higher education (yes/no); formal income (yes/no).Psychosocial variables: previous diagnosis of mpox (yes/no); knowing people close who were diagnosed with mpox (yes/no); intimate contact with a person diagnosed with mpox (yes/no); would disclose mpox serological status (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by health services (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by friends (yes/no); fear of being discriminated against by family (yes/no); belief that someone may face homophobia because of mpox (yes/no).Behavioral variables: type of sexual partnership (last six months) (no partner/fixed/fixed+casual); was immunized against COVID-19 (yes/no); stopped engaging in casual sex after the mpox outbreak (yes/no); would undergo pre- and post-exposure testing for mpox (yes/no); condomless sexual practice (yes/no); uses apps to seek sex (yes/no); uses saunas to seek sex (yes/no); seeks sex in public places (parties and clubs) (yes/no); use of glory hole (yes/no); practice of chemsex (yes/no); practice of cruising (yes/no); practice of bugchasing (yes/no); challenging sexual practices (yes/no); and participation in orgies (yes/no).The following practices were defined based on previous studies [16,18]: (a) double penetration: simultaneous sexual penetration by two or more penises; (b) challenging sexual practice: consistent engagement in two or three of these practices, defined based on the circumstances in which they occur; (c) fisting or footing: anal penetration using the fist or foot; (d) cruising: free, consensual, and anonymous sex practiced between men in public spaces, such as parks, wooded areas, beaches, or parking lots; (e) glory hole: a round opening in a wall that allows insertion of the penis, so that someone on the other side can use it sexually in various ways; (f) bugchasing: when an HIV-negative man deliberately seeks an HIV-positive man to become infected. To define chemsex, participants were asked whether they had used illicit drugs immediately before and/or during sexual intercourse in the past 12 months. For those who answered yes, a multiple-choice list was presented to indicate the specific drugs used [18].BiasTo reduce selection bias, the virtual snowball technique was adopted, favoring the inclusion of participants from different regions, sociodemographic profiles, and sexual contexts. The questionnaire underwent face and content validation and pilot testing, which minimized measurement bias. Online data collection allowed for greater anonymity, reducing underreporting of stigmatized practices.Study sizeSample size calculation was performed using G*Power software, version 3.1.9.7, considering the population of men aged >18 years in Brazil. The assumed prevalence was 50% (to maximize sample size due to the lack of prior data on this phenomenon), with a tolerable standard error of 3% and a 95% confidence level. The estimated sample size at the end was 1,067 men.Statistical methodsStatistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS software (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA), version 27.0. An exploratory analysis was performed to describe the distribution of predictor variables in relation to health vulnerability behavior, with data presented as absolute and relative frequencies.Pearson’s chi-square test was used to assess the association between predictor variables and adherence to health vulnerability behaviors and to screen candidate variables for the initial multivariable model. Variables with p-value<0.020 in the bivariate analysis were considered eligible to compose this model.The presence of multicollinearity was investigated using tolerance coefficients and the variance inflation factor (VIF). The final stage of the analysis consisted of multivariable modeling to identify factors independently associated with health vulnerability behavior among men who have sex with men. The generalized linear Poisson regression model was applied with a log link function because the outcome prevalence was >10%. Adherence to the Poisson distribution was assessed using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (p-value>0.005) and the assumption of equidispersion. The calculation of adjusted prevalence ratios (APR) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) used the hybrid parameter estimation method, the robust variance estimator, and Type III analysis to test model effects. The omnibus test was used to evaluate the hypothesis of the final multivariable model, which explains factors associated with health vulnerability behavior, against a model containing only the intercept, at a significance level of 5% (p-value<0.005). The final model was adjusted for age and showed a good fit to the data (deviance 771.862; AIC 1.187.862; BIC 1.219.517; log-likelihood –587.931). The omnibus test indicated that the overall model was significant (χ2(5)=23.048; p-value<0.001). The significance of the APR for variables included in the final model was assessed using the Wald chi-square test, with variables having p-values<0.005 considered significant. ResultsAmong study participants, 13.9% (n=202) of the 1,449 men who reported having sex with men presented at least one health vulnerability behavior, while 86.1% (n=1,247) reported none of these behaviors. Among vulnerable participants, 17.3% (n=35/202) presented two or more vulnerability behaviors. Specifically, 50.4% (n=102/202) reported that they would not be vaccinated against mpox, 30.6% (n=62/202) stated that they would not take self-care/contact notification measures, 26.2% (n=53/202) that they would not undergo mpox testing, and 9.9% (n=20/202) reported that they would not follow treatment if diagnosed (Table 1).Table 1Distribution of health vulnerability behaviors among men who have sex with men in the context of mpox.
